challenger_routes.why_considered: A goal of the form 'Write the text T to the file X and save the report to Y' returned status PASS__COMPOSED_CAPABILITY_CHAIN with pass=True after writing those 11 bytes into Y. X, the file the goal actually named, was never created on disk and the front door reported the goal done. The gate that catches this, promised_artifact_errors, had already run; its result was discarded.
challenger_routes.why_not_selected_or_selected: SELECTED: apply the gate that already exists to the fallback before it may report success. Two supporting defects were found by measuring the same family. (1) Template key order for the repair capabilities is output_path, source_root, test_argv, test_paths, and test_argv is derived FROM the test paths, so counting a derived argv as a competing claim cancelled the role against itself: exclusivity emptied a correct test_paths, the fallback then assigned every file in the sentence, source included. (2) That masking hid a second defect: _repo_paths only checks that a path RESOLVES under the root, so 'test command /usr/bin/python3 T' bound usr/bin/python3 as a test file and the adapter rejected it with FILE_INVALID. Both are fixed generally: an argv is not a claim, and a role list may only name files that exist. Measured: the false PASS becomes FAIL_CLOSED__PROMISED_ARTIFACT_MISSING naming the exact missing file; test_paths on the route-admission sentence returns exactly the named test; test_paths on the strict-progress sentence returns exactly the named test with no interpreter. Benchmark unchanged at 23/23 compiled and 22/23 selected. Repair-family end-to-end pass rate unchanged at 1 of 6, which is stated rather than hidden: the remaining cause is the deliberate no-write-authority boundary.

challenger_routes.why_not_selected_or_selected: SELECTED: separate the two acts. Refusing keeps the one-word rule. Taking over a route now requires the caller's WHOLE name, in order, in PROSE -- repository paths and identifier tokens are stripped first, a trailing version token is optional because prose drops it, and among several names stated the MOST SPECIFIC one wins. Measured in three steps over the same 13 path-style receipt-backed targets: 6 of 13 before, 10 of 13 once the whole name was required (the 3 remaining lost to a SIBLING, because 'bytes characteristic active query task generator v10' also states the whole of bytes_active_query_task_generator_v1 with one extra word in the middle), and 13 of 13 once specificity decides.
